question.prompt: At \(2{:}15\) o’clock, the hour and minute hands of a clock form an angle of:

solutions.explanation:
The hour hand moves steadily between hour marks, so at \(2{:}15\) it has already moved beyond \(2\). Adjacent hour marks are separated by \(360^\circ/12=30^\circ\).

The minute hand points to \(3\). Since \(15\) minutes is \(15/60=\frac14\) of an hour, the hour hand is one quarter of the way from \(2\) to \(3\). The smaller angle between the hands is the remaining three quarters of that interval:
\[
\frac34\cdot30^\circ=22\frac12^\circ.
\]
The answer is choice C.
solutions.title: Track the hour hand between marks
